judge_assessment.explanation: The ACCEPT survives independent checking. Bar-graph values recompute to Cleo 12, total 31 and a Cleo-minus-Ben difference of 7; the line plot (2 at 3in, 5 at 4in, 3 at 5in, 1 at 6in, 1 at 7in) gives 5 pencils at exactly 4 inches, 12 in the cup, range 4, mode 4 and 5 pencils longer than 4 inches; the shape tally is 1 triangle, 4 quadrilaterals, 0 pentagons, 1 hexagon, which I verified against the TikZ source (P square, Q rectangle, R rhombus, S trapezoid, T triangle, U hexagon). The judge did not state problem 11's answer, so I checked it separately: a 6 cm square has perimeter 24, an 8 x 3 rectangle has perimeter 22, difference 2 cm, which matches the check. Both open responses are honestly manual (problem 8's 'why is Dev wrong' and problem 12(b)'s more-than-half argument), and problem 12(a)'s count is checked separately as 4 + 1 = 5. I tested the two dominant systemic failures against this case and neither applies: problem 5's four-row tally chart carries FOUR read_data entries, one per printed row, and every open response is typed manual.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 5's tally chart prints four rows (3, 4, 5 and 6 sides) and verify.json declares four separate read_data entries under id 5, one per row, including the 0 for pentagons. This is per-slot verification done correctly, and the deliberate zero row is what makes the sort a classification rather than a count of the shapes that happen to be there.

Problem 12 splits its own parts across the trust boundary: (a) 'how many of them have exactly 4 sides' is an eval check (4 + 1 = 5) and (b) 'Is Ben right? Use numbers to explain' is a manual entry whose desc tells the reviewer what a correct comparison looks like (5 against half of 7). One problem, two response types, two correctly typed entries.

The three displays are shared across all twelve problems instead of each problem carrying its own figure, and the bar-graph and line-plot `data` objects in verify.json are the same values that draw the pgfplots figure, so a reader and the checker cannot disagree about what the graph shows.

final_response.md is the model delivery message in this run: it names all three PDFs with page counts, states which two items are manual and why, and documents two layout defects that were found by rendering the PDF rather than by a gate (pgfplots rotating the first bar's label onto the y-axis, and \answerline inside a \problem stem printing above the workspace instead of below it). That second note is reusable knowledge.
case_summary: An accept I can confirm in full. Twelve interleaved problems genuinely mix bar-graph reading, line-plot reading, data measures and shape classification, every objective subpart recomputes correctly, and the two open responses are typed manual with reviewer criteria rather than being folded into the machine-verified count. Two things make this case the reference for the run: problem 5's four-row tally chart declares one check per printed row, which is exactly the per-slot coverage seven of my ten cases are missing, and problem 12 splits into an eval for the count and a manual entry for the reasoning. The delivery message names all three artifacts with their compiled page counts and records two rendering defects found by looking at the PDF. No defect worth recording.
